entries.homeLine: Agents now ask before every change until an Admin lets them start work on their own.
lines: Agents set to Auto or Full auto could change your work before anyone on the team had looked.
Agent work now starts on I approve first: each change an agent makes waits for a person, whatever its mode.
Nothing changes without your team, and the setting shows who changed it last and when.
To let agents work in their own mode again, an Admin picks Agent starts on its own on the Today card's gear.

entries.homeLine: After a change, Chat can check back on a later day and tell you what happened.
lines: It was easy to fix a page and never learn whether the fix worked.
After a change, Chat offers a check in 7, 14, 30 or 90 days that reads your tracking data.
You get Improved, No meaningful change or Declined in the chat and at the top of your Inbox.
Click Set check on the card Chat shows after a change you made or approved.

entries.homeLine: Chat can now do work on a schedule, such as a report every Monday at 9:00.
lines: Weekly reports and checks meant asking Chat the same thing every week.
Say "every Monday at 9:00" and Chat shows a card you can edit; nothing is scheduled until you click.
Each run lands in your Inbox or your email, and a repeat can say No change when nothing moved.
Admins and Managers ask in any chat, then manage their jobs on the Scheduled page in the Chat menu.

entries.homeLine: Pick your own time zone, so Chat's times and your schedules match your day.
lines: Times followed your browser, which was off when you travel or work in another time zone.
Each person can now pick a time zone, or keep Automatic to follow the browser.
New scheduled jobs, Chat's times and your daily suggestions use it.
Open Settings › Account › Time zone and type a city or an offset.

entries.feature: Agents that publish on their own
entries.homeLine: An Admin can now let chosen agents publish pages without waiting for a click.
lines: Routine pages waited for a click even when the agent's work was ready.
With an Admin's two switches, an agent in Full auto sends or publishes up to the daily limit you set.
A page still waits for you when it fails Quality, your brand facts or the other safety checks.
Turn on Agents that publish on their own in Settings › Chat, then allow it on the agent.

entries.homeLine: Chat answers questions from your Ansvisor data and does the work with you.
lines: Finding an answer about your AI visibility meant opening page after page.
Chat reads your data, shows each step it takes and asks before it changes anything.
You get answers, drafts and reports in one place, with the numbers checked against your data.
Ask a question on Chat Home, or press Ctrl J to open Chat beside any page.

entries.homeLine: See what each brand has connected, and what it could connect, right in Chat.
lines: Connected tools were spread across settings, so it was hard to see what a brand had.
Connections lists each tool with its status, account and the skills and agents that use it.
You see what a tool would unlock before you connect it, and what would stop if you disconnect it.
Open Connections in the Chat menu; an Admin connects a tool, and others ask their Admin.

entries.homeLine: Chat can remember short notes between chats, such as the tone your brand uses.
lines: Repeating the same preferences in every chat took time.
Start a message with "Remember that…" and Chat saves one short line once you click Save.
Notes for you, a brand or the workspace shape every chat, and the steps show when one was used.
Change or delete notes on the Memory page, from the ⋯ menu at the top of a chat.

entries.homeLine: Open Skills to run, schedule or turn off Chat's skills, and keep your own.
lines: A good way of doing a task was hard to repeat the same way every time.
The Skills page lists Ansvisor's skills and your own, each with the connections it uses.
Admins and Managers can save steps as a skill in Chat, or import one from a file or GitHub for review.
Open Skills in the Chat menu, or type / in Chat to use a skill.

entries.homeLine: A page published through Ansvisor can be taken down from the Library in one click.
lines: Pulling a page that went live used to mean finding it in your CMS.
Take down removes a page from your Webflow, WordPress or Wix site and keeps it there as a draft.
A page you took down never goes live on its own again, even from an agent.
Admins and Managers pick Take down in the page's … menu in the Library, or on an agent's notice.

entries.homeLine: Chat Home now fits the work you do, from content to competitors.
lines: A content lead and a founder need different things from the same data.
Pick your focus once and Chat Home shows your shortcuts, starter questions and new skills.
You start from the questions that matter to you, filled with your own competitors and topics.
Click the focus pill on Chat Home to pick or change your areas.

entries.homeLine: Chat prepares this week's Action Center tasks and tracks them under its answer.
lines: Action Center tells you what to do, but the work still took hours.
Chat drafts the work for the tasks due this week and attaches it to each task.
You review finished drafts instead of starting from a blank page.
Click Complete tasks on Chat Home, then attach each draft to its task and mark it done.

entries.homeLine: Agent Center runs your routine AI visibility work on a schedule or when something changes.
lines: Weekly checks and fixes took the same hours every week.
An agent runs a skill on a schedule or when Action Center finds a signal, within its share of your AI limit.
The routine work gets done, and you choose which changes wait for your approval.
Open Agent Center and pick a ready-made agent, or build your own in four steps.

entries.homeLine: Each morning your Inbox suggests one thing worth doing for your brand.
lines: With many pages and prompts, it is hard to know where to start each day.
Every morning Chat picks one suggestion for you and your brand, with the data behind it.
You spend your time on the change most likely to win AI answers.
Open Inbox, then open the suggestion in the Content Editor or do it with Chat.

entries.homeLine: Ask Chat why a metric moved and see what changed it, part by part.
lines: A drop in visibility rarely says why it happened.
Chat compares two periods of your tracking and shows how much each cause explains.
You know whether a change is real or normal swing before you act on it.
Ask "Why did my visibility drop?" or click Why? under Since you left on Chat Home.
